name: Storybook Lantern
tagline: Hand-cut paper shapes, a warm glow and a slow parallax drift from night to sunset.
description: Soft illustrated storybook on grainy paper: flat shapes with slightly rough edges, a muted teal, brick red, dusk purple and lamp-yellow palette, and gentle glows. A slow narrative told in layered parallax scenes with soft crossfades, springy icon pops and one handwritten closing line. Made for warm brand stories, app origin tales and gentle explainers. The preview follows a small figure and a glowing teapot spirit.

display.usage: One handwritten closing line, 84–96px, cream #fff3d9 with a soft plum shadow, revealed by a left-to-right wipe

body.usage: Tiny in-world lettering such as the kiosk sign, 30–36px, never a headline

transitions: 0.7–0.8s opacity crossfade between scenes, the next scene fading in while the previous one keeps panning
no cuts, wipes or slams; every scene is already moving when it appears
textAnimations: single handwritten line revealed with clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0 0% 0 0), 1.5s, power1.inOut
no per-letter bounce; text arrives like ink being written

rhythm.notes: Five beats of about 1.5–2.5s: desk, star, dawn walk, rooftop, sunset drift. Something small and new (an icon spring, a pointing spout, a bird, a rising heart) happens every ~1s while the camera never stops drifting.

guide:
- Look only: build the user's own subject in this visual language; don't reuse the example's scene.
- Build every scene from flat SVG shapes (no outlines) in muted teal #4a8f8e / #2f6b6d, brick red #b4483a, dusk purple #5b4690 / #2a2452, lamp-yellow #f6c75a and warm peach/pink sky tones (#f6cfa4, #ee9d7c). Apply one shared filter on each layer SVG: feTurbulence baseFrequency 0.026, numOctaves 2, feDisplacementMap scale 7 for a rough hand-cut edge.
- Add a paper layer on top of everything: fractalNoise (baseFrequency 0.85) tinted warm brown at 0.5 opacity, a low-frequency mottling layer at 0.16, and a plum radial vignette. Never use plain gradients without that grain.
- Give every scene 3–4 parallax layers (sky, far, mid, near) panning at different speeds with sine.inOut (e.g. -60 / -130 / -300 / -620px over 2.3s) plus a 4–7% camera scale push. Nothing ever stops moving.
- Light comes from one small glowing source: a radial gradient glow (r 170, #ffd678 at 0.75 → 0) that bobs ±20px with sine.inOut. Keep figures small (about 240px tall in a 1080px frame); limbs swing ±20° with sine.inOut yoyo.
- Small icons (#ee7f97 hearts, #8fa8c8 rain, stars, ideas) pop in from scale 0 with elastic.out(1,0.5) over 0.8–1s, then rise 300–500px with a small sine sway and fade; stagger them 0.11s. Something small and new happens about every second.
- Tell it in 4–5 scenes of 1.5–2.5s joined by 0.7–0.8s opacity crossfades, the next scene fading in while the previous one keeps panning. Colour temperature warms scene by scene, night purple toward sunset peach.
- Text is rare: in-world lettering in Patrick Hand 30–36px, and at most one handwritten line (Kalam 700, 84–96px, cream #fff3d9 with a soft plum shadow) wiped in left to right with clip-path over 1.5s, power1.inOut.
- Optional motif: a tiny luminous companion that travels with the subject and lights each scene. Avoid hard cuts, bouncy overshoot on big shapes, glossy gradients and more than one line of text.
example: The preview follows a small figure and a glowing teapot spirit from a night desk past a star, down a dawn street and over rooftops into a sunset, ending on the line 'Small lights still find the way.' Don't copy this scene unless asked.
